facts.text: A safety case is a structured written argument supported by evidence that a system is acceptably safe for a stated use in a stated environment; the safety argument is the reasoning connecting the evidence to the claim.
facts.quote: A safety case is a structured written argument, supported by evidence, that a system is acceptably safe for a stated use in a stated environment, and the safety argument is the reasoning that connects the evidence to the claim.

facts.text: The booklet characterizes a safety case as claims plus reasoning plus evidence within a stated context and set of assumptions, rather than a pile of test reports.
facts.quote: a safety case is claims plus reasoning plus evidence within a stated context and set of assumptions, "not a pile of test reports" [Chapter 12]

facts.text: A safety case organizes its top-level claim into sub-claims that all hazards are identified and controlled, the control chain meets its required reliability level, perception is adequate across the operating envelope, and the right authority has accepted residual risk.
facts.quote: Below it, sub-claims: all hazards are identified; each is controlled; the control chain meets its required reliability level; perception is adequate across the operating envelope; the residual risk has been accepted by the right authority.

facts.text: Safety-case evidence includes hazard analysis, failure tables, test results, correlation reports and field data.
facts.quote: At the bottom sits the evidence: hazard analysis, failure tables, test results, correlation reports, field data.

facts.text: A safety case records its machine, site and speed context and its assumptions because validity in a dry quarry does not establish validity in a snowy mine.
facts.quote: The context (which machines, sites, speeds) and the assumptions are written down, because a case true for a dry quarry may be false for a snowy mine.

facts.text: Mature safety cases record defeaters—the reasons the argument could be wrong—and how each defeater was answered.
facts.quote: Mature cases also record defeaters, the reasons the argument could be wrong, and how each was answered [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet proposes that the program's top-level safety-case claim should establish that, within machine configuration M, operating envelope E and safety-function scope F, the defined virtual-test process produces evidence credible enough to support engineering decision D with explicitly bounded residual uncertainty.
facts.quote: Within machine configuration M, operating envelope E and safety-function scope F, the defined virtual-test process produces evidence credible enough to support engineering decision D with explicitly bounded residual uncertainty.

facts.text: The booklet breaks the program's proposed safety-case claim into ten sub-claims, each paired with evidence the roadmap must create; these include valid intended use, simulation representing the real system, evidence remaining inside the validated domain, and conclusions following from evidence.
facts.quote: It breaks this into ten sub-claims, each paired with the evidence the roadmap must create, from "the intended use is valid" and "the simulation represents the real system" to "evidence stays inside the validated domain" and "conclusions follow from the evidence" [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The booklet's preferred safety argument uses physical testing to establish anchors and boundaries, independent validation to show prediction of safety-relevant quantities with known uncertainty within those boundaries, simulation to cover the interior, and targeted physical confirmation at high-risk boundaries and after influential changes.
facts.quote: physical testing established the anchors and boundaries; independent validation showed the simulation predicts the safety-relevant quantities with known uncertainty inside them; the model then covered the interior; targeted physical confirmation stayed at the high-risk boundaries and after influential changes

facts.text: The Nimrod Review (2009) showed that a safety case can become paperwork that nobody challenges.
facts.quote: The Nimrod Review (2009) showed that a safety case can become paperwork nobody challenges

facts.text: A safety-case diagram can become an impressive-looking justification for an unsupported premise.
facts.quote: a diagram "can become an impressive-looking justification for an unsupported premise"

facts.text: The booklet found no evidence that any safety-case notation improves heavy-machinery outcomes; the value of safety-case notation for this program is structuring what the evidence must show.
facts.quote: no evidence was found that any notation improves heavy-machinery outcomes. Its value here is structuring what the evidence must show [Chapter 12].

facts.text: The lawyer reviewer recommends writing the safety case as if an opposing expert will read it, stating simulation validity limits, and preserving all raw data and model versions.
facts.quote: The lawyer reviewer adds: write it as if an opposing expert will read it, state the validity limits of the simulation, and preserve all raw data and model versions [Chapter 13].

facts.text: The illustrated automatic-braking safety case claims acceptable safety for machine family M inside operating envelope E and supports identification and control of missed-intervention and unsafe-intervention hazards with hazard and risk analysis approved before the prototype.
facts.quote: A1["Argument: hazards of missed and unsafe intervention are identified and controlled"]

facts.text: The illustrated automatic-braking safety case supports the claim that the braking chain meets its required Machine Performance Level with FMEDA, fault-injection results and software verification.
facts.quote: A2 --> E2["Evidence: FMEDA, fault-injection results, software verification"]

facts.text: The illustrated automatic-braking safety case supports perception adequacy across conditions inside operating envelope E with detection rates on real data binned by dust, rain, snow and light.
facts.quote: A3 --> E3["Evidence: detection rates on real data, binned by dust, rain, snow, light"]

facts.text: The illustrated automatic-braking safety case supports using virtual evidence only inside its validated envelope with a correlation report, a credibility assessment and physical confirmation tests at envelope boundaries.
facts.quote:
A4 --> E4["Evidence: correlation report and credibility assessment"]
    A4 --> E5["Evidence: physical confirmation tests at the envelope boundaries"]

facts.text: The booklet concludes that the defensible route for a four-month validation is an analytical safety case plus targeted physical tests, with simulation presented under a credibility framework.
facts.quote: The booklet concludes that the defensible route for a four-month validation is an analytical safety case plus targeted physical tests, with simulation presented under a credibility framework [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The program's safety case will be read by the safety board, a notified body, mining customers and, if something goes wrong, a court.
facts.quote: The safety case is what the safety board, a notified body, mining customers and, if something goes wrong, a court will read.
